definition: Spatial intelligence is a term used in artificial intelligence research to describe systems capable of perceiving, understanding, reasoning about, generating, and interacting with three-dimensional physical and virtual environments.
details: It emphasizes "world models" that incorporate spatial relationships, geometry, physics, and dynamics, in contrast to text- or image-centric models. The concept has been prominently advocated by computer scientist Fei-Fei Li, who has described it as a necessary next step for artificial intelligence beyond large language models. Li co-founded World Labs in 2024 to develop related technologies.

explainer.lead: Spatial intelligence describes AI systems that can perceive, understand, reason about, generate, and act within 3D physical or virtual environments. It matters because it shifts focus from text- and image-centric models toward world models grounded in geometry and physics.

tiers.eli5: Most AI today reads and writes; spatial intelligence is about an AI that can also picture a room, know where things are, and figure out how to move around them.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build world models that encode geometry, physics, and dynamics so agents can plan in 3D space. A pitfall is that text- and image-centric pretraining supplies little of the spatial grounding these models need.
tiers.paperLevel: No single formal definition is given; the term refers to systems combining perception, understanding, reasoning, generation, and interaction over 3D environments, typically via world models incorporating spatial relationships, geometry, physics, and dynamics.

explainer.example: A robot asked to fetch a cup would use a spatial world model to locate the cup in the room, judge distances and obstacles, and plan a path rather than only describing the scene in words.
